chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) passed by the lepers while he was riding his donkey, and they were eating lunch. So they invited him to lunch. He said: 'Indeed, if I were not fasting, I would have done so.' When he returned to his house, he ordered food to be prepared, and he ordered that they should be refined/elegant in it. Then he invited them, so they had lunch with him, and he had lunch with them.

key_terms.يَتَنَوَّقُوا: to be refined/elegant (in preparation or manner)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn do when he passed by lepers while fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical humility of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), who, despite being a revered scholar and descendant of the Prophet, did not let his status or fasting prevent him from engaging intimately with the marginalized. By inviting the lepers to his home and ensuring the food was prepared with care ('tanaqqaw'), he demonstrated that true nobility lies in serving others, a key virtue in Shia ethical teachings. The narrative highlights the balance between personal devotion (fasting) and social responsibility (hospitality), showing that spiritual rank does not isolate one from the community.
